'''Galen Edward Mitchell''' "'''Tolu'''" '''Smith III''' (born July 26, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]] and [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State Bulldogs]].

==High school career==
Smith was raised in [[Bay St. Louis, Mississippi]], and played basketball at Bay High School.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jevan|last=McCoskey|title=Former Mississippi State basketball star Tolu Smith returns to Bay St. Louis to speak with Bay-Waveland middle school basketball team|url=https://www.wxxv25.com/former-mississippi-state-basketball-star-tolu-smith-returns-to-bay-st-louis-to-speak-with-bay-waveland-middle-school-basketball-team/|website=WXXV25.com|date=August 15, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> He moved with his family to Hawaii in 2017 and enrolled at [[Kahuku High & Intermediate School]] in [[Kahuku, Hawaii|Kahuku]] for his senior season.<ref name=abramo17nov21/> He was selected as the ''[[Honolulu Star-Advertiser]]'' All-State player of the year in 2018.<ref name=honda20>{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Honda|title=Life after Kahuku: Tolu Smith thriving at Mississippi State|url=https://www.hawaiiprepworld.com/boys-basketball/life-after-kahuku-tolu-smith-thriving-at-mississippi-state/|work=Hawaii Prep World|date=December 24, 2020|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
Smith played his freshman season for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]] and averaged 3.3 points and 2.6 rebounds per game.<ref name=honda20/> He elected to transfer at the end of the season to join his home state [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State Bulldogs]].<ref name=honda20/> Smith sat out the 2019–20 season due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) transfer rules.<ref name=krajisnik24>{{cite web|first=Stefan|last=Krajisnik|title=How Tolu Smith has overcome injury to build powerful legacy at Mississippi State basketball|url=https://eu.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/mississippi-state/2024/03/07/tolu-smith-mississippi-state-basketball-legacy-injury-chris-jans-shannel-galen-bulldogs/72807119007/|work=Clarion Ledger|date=March 7, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref>

Smith appeared in 30 games during his sophomore season but only started 20 during his junior season as he battled multiple injuries.<ref name=krajisnik24/> He returned to full health for his senior season in 2022–23 and started all 34 games.<ref name=krajisnik24/> Smith averaged 15.7 points with a league-leading 57.2% field goal percentage to earn first-team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) honors.<ref name=krajisnik23>{{cite web|first=Stefan|last=Krajisnik|title=Tolu Smith, Mississippi State basketball's All-SEC forward, announces 2023-24 decision|url=https://eu.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/mississippi-state/2023/05/21/tolu-smith-mississippi-state-basketball-returning-2023-nba-draft-chris-jans/70241359007/|work=Clarion Ledger|date=May 21, 2023|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> He declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] but returned to Mississippi State for his fifth year of collegiate eligibility.<ref name=krajisnik23/> Smith averaged 15 points and 8 rebounds per game during the 2023–24 season and was named to the All-SEC first-team.<ref>{{cite web|first=Rob|last=DeMello|title=Kahuku’s Tolu Smith awaits hopeful NBA opportunity|url=https://www.khon2.com/sports/kahukus-tolu-smith-awaits-nba-opportunity/|work=KHON 2|date=June 26, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Smith joined the [[Detroit Pistons]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Benjamin|last=Rosenberg|title=Four former Mississippi State players taking talents to NBA Summer League|url=https://cdispatch.com/sports/four-former-mississippi-state-players-taking-talents-to-nba-summer-league/|work=The Dispatch|date=July 17, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> and on September 17, 2024, he signed with the team.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Pistons Sign Three Players To Camp Contracts|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/pistons-sign-three-players-to-camp-contracts.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 18, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> However, he was waived on October 17<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has waived Aaron Estrada, Javante McCoy, Dereon Seabron, Tolu Smith, and Lamar Stevens. Detroit’s roster now stands at 15, including one two-way contract.|number=1847054117455442163|user=Pistons_PR|date=October 17, 2024|access-date=October 17, 2024}}</ref> and on October 29, he joined the [[Motor City Cruise]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Motor City Cruise|title=Training camp roster ready to get to it 👏 #MotorCityBasketball|number=1851401150169223597|user=MotorCityCruise|date=October 29, 2024|access-date=November 4, 2024}}</ref> On January 6, 2025, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Pistons.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today that the team has signed Ron Harper Jr. and Tolu Smith to two-way contracts. Per team policy, terms of the agreement were not disclosed. In a related move, the Pistons waived forward Cole Swider and guard Alondes Williams.|number=1876388325537497524|user=Pistons_PR|date=January 6, 2025|access-date=January 7, 2025}}</ref> On April 13, Smith made his NBA debut against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the final game of the regular season and scored 14 points with 8 rebounds.<ref name=demello>{{cite web |last1=DeMello |first1=Rob |title=Kahuku’s Tolu Smith makes NBA debut |url=https://www.khon2.com/sports/kahukus-tolu-smith-makes-nba-debut/ |website=KHON2 |access-date=April 14, 2025 |date=April 13, 2025}}</ref> He became the second Hawaii high school graduate to appear in an NBA game after [[Red Rocha]] who last played in 1957.<ref name=demello/>

On April 7, 2026, the Pistons signed Smith to a two-year, standard contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pistons sign two-way center Tolu Smith to roster, wave Bobi Klintman|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2026/04/07/pistons-nba-roster-tolu-smith-bobi-klintman/89504891007/|access-date=April 17, 2026|website=freep.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Smith was born to an African-American father and Samoan mother.<ref name=abramo17nov21/> His father, Galen, worked as a computer specialist for the [[Naval Oceanographic Office]],<ref name=abramo17nov21>{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Abramo|title=Kahuku welcomes major hoops talent in Smith|url=https://www.hawaiiprepworld.com/boys-basketball/kahuku-welcomes-major-hoops-talent-in-smith/|work=Hawaii Prep World|date=November 21, 2017|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> and previously played college basketball in the United States Virgin Islands.<ref name=magee>{{cite web|first=Patrick|last=Magee|title=Towering, talented: Smith brothers have Bay High eyeing title run|url=https://www.sunherald.com/sports/high-school/article132057399.html|website=SunHerald.com|date=February 11, 2017|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> Smith's mother, Shannel, played basketball for the [[South Alabama Jaguars women's basketball|South Alabama Jaguars]].<ref name=magee/> His older brother, Galen Jr., played basketball for the [[Xavier Gold Rush and Gold Nuggets|Xavier Gold Rush]].<ref name=abramo17nov13>{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Abramo|title=Kahuku transfer Smith signs with WKU|url=https://www.hawaiiprepworld.com/boys-basketball/kahuku-transfer-smith-signs-with-wku/|work=Hawaii Prep World|date=November 13, 2017|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref>

Smith's nickname, "Tolu", means "three" in [[Samoan language|Samoan]] as he was the third Galen in his family.<ref name=honda18>{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Honda|title=Q&A: Kahuku hoopster, All-State POY Tolu Smith |url=https://www.hawaiiprepworld.com/boys-basketball/qa-kahuku-hoopster-all-state-poy-tolu-smith/|work=Hawaii Prep World|date=March 20, 2018|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> He received his initials, G.E.M.S., because his parents considered him and his brother to be their "gems".<ref name=honda18/>
